newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hyundai Motor to reopen plants.
newsitem.headline: Hyundai Motor to reopen plants.

text.p: Hyundai Motor Co Ltd, South Korea's largest carmaker, said on Friday it would reopen its plants on Saturday after a week of temporary shutdown.
The shutdown followed two weeks of wildcat strikes by union workers protesting at a controversial labour law.
Hyundai Motor said the strikes and the shutdown cost the company 78,000 cars in lost production and 650 billion won in lost sales.
"The suspension of production ... not only caused difficulties with the company's business but also pushed many part suppliers to the brink of bankruptcy," a company statement said.
Hyundai Motor workers have been at the forefront of the strikes that started on December 26 when the ruling party rammed the labour bill through parliament.
The law allows companies to lay off workers, replace striking workers and change working hours.
